questions.prompt:
What exact output does code example 1 in this lesson produce?

def add_item(value: str, items: list[str] | None = None) -> list[str]:
    if items is None:
        items = []
    items.append(value)
    return items

print(add_item('a'))
print(add_item('b'))
questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`def add_item(value: str, items: list[str] | None = None) -> list[str]:` — Creates reusable behavior; without the definition, callers cannot invoke or share this rule.
`if items is None:` — Selects behavior for a condition; without branches, different cases follow the same path.
`items = []` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`items.append(value)` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
`return items` — Sends a result to the caller; without it, a function usually returns None.
`print(add_item('a'))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
`print(add_item('b'))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

questions.prompt: Which statement accurately describes “Mutable default arguments in functions”?
options: Syntax and indentation mark code-block boundaries; a mistake can prevent a route or condition from running.
Comments explain a non-obvious decision instead of repeating the code, such as why a particular limit was chosen.
A default expression is evaluated once when the function is defined.
Python is used for automation, web services, and data analysis because its readable syntax and broad library ecosystem make small, testable steps practical.
questions.answer: A default expression is evaluated once when the function is defined.
questions.explanation: A default expression is evaluated once when the function is defined. A mutable list, dict, or set can therefore become shared state across calls. Use a `None` sentinel and create a fresh object per call. If sharing is intentional, make it explicit rather than hiding it in a default.
